sanskrit: na cet paritrāsya imāñ janān bhayād; dviṣadbhir evaṃ balibhiḥ prapīḍitān tathābhaviṣyad dviṣatāṃ pramodanaṃ; yathā hateṣv eṣv iha no 'riṣu tvayā
english: Had you not rescued these folk from their terror, hard-pressed as they were by such mighty foes, the joy of our enemies would have been as great as our own joy now is, when you have slain these foes of ours here.

sanskrit: itīva bhūyaś ca suhṛdbhir īritā; niśamya vācaḥ sumanās tato 'rjunaḥ yathānurūpaṃ pratipūjya taṃ janaṃ; jagāma saṃśaptakasaṃghahā punaḥ
english: Hearing such words and yet more spoken by his comrades, Arjuna, glad at heart, honored those people as was fitting, and then, the slayer of the host of the Saṃśaptakas, set forth once more.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca pratyāgatya punar jiṣṇur ahan saṃśaptakān bahūn vakrānuvakragamanād aṅgāraka iva grahaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Returning once again, the victorious one slew many of the Saṃśaptakas, moving with crooked turns and counter-turns like the planet Aṅgāraka.

sanskrit: pārthabāṇahatā rājan narāśvarathakuñjarāḥ vicelur babhramur neduḥ petur mamluś ca māriṣa
english: Struck by Pārtha's arrows, O king, men, horses, chariots, and elephants reeled, wheeled about, cried out, fell, and wilted, good sir.

sanskrit: dhuryaṃ dhuryatarān sūtān rathāṃś ca parisaṃkṣipan pāṇīn pāṇigataṃ śastraṃ bāhūn api śirāṃsi ca
english: The Pāṇḍava cut down draft-beasts, sturdier draft-beasts, drivers, and chariots, and likewise hands, the weapons in those hands, arms too, and heads,

sanskrit: bhallaiḥ kṣurair ardhacandrair vatsadantaiś ca pāṇḍavaḥ cicchedāmitravīrāṇāṃ samare pratiyudhyatām
english: with broad-headed shafts, razor-arrows, crescent-points, and calf-tooth barbs—the heads of the hostile warriors who fought against him in battle.

sanskrit: vāśitārthe yuyutsanto vṛṣabhā vṛṣabhaṃ yathā āpatanty arjunaṃ śūrāḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: As bulls eager to fight over a cow rush upon a rival bull, so the heroes fell upon Arjuna by hundreds and by thousands.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tasya ca tad yuddham abhaval lomaharṣaṇam trailokyavijaye yādṛg daityānāṃ saha vajriṇā
english: The battle between them and him was such as to make the hair stand on end, like that of the Daityas with the wielder of the thunderbolt in the conquest of the three worlds.

sanskrit: tam avidhyat tribhir bāṇair dandaśūkair ivāhibhiḥ ugrāyudhas tatas tasya śiraḥ kāyād apāharat
english: A warrior of fierce weapons pierced him with three arrows, like venomous biting serpents; thereupon Arjuna struck that man's head from his body.

sanskrit: te 'rjunaṃ sarvataḥ kruddhā nānāśastrair avīvṛṣan marudbhiḥ preṣitā meghā himavantam ivoṣṇage
english: Enraged, they rained down on Arjuna from every side with weapons of every kind, as clouds driven by the Maruts pour upon the Himavat in the hot season.

sanskrit: astrair astrāṇi saṃvārya dviṣatāṃ sarvato 'rjunaḥ samyag astaiḥ śaraiḥ sarvān sahitān ahanad bahūn
english: Warding off the enemies' weapons on all sides with his own weapons, Arjuna, with well-aimed shafts, slew all those many foes together.

sanskrit: chinnatriveṇujaṅgheṣān nihatapārṣṇisārathīn saṃchinnaraśmiyoktrākṣān vyanukarṣayugān rathān vidhvastasarvasaṃnāhān bāṇaiś cakre 'rjunas tvaran
english: With their triple bamboo poles, shafts, and supports severed, their flank-guards and drivers slain, their reins, traces, and axles cut, their draw-bars and yokes broken, and all their gear shattered—such did Arjuna swiftly make the chariots with his arrows.

sanskrit: te rathās tatra vidhvastāḥ parārdhyā bhānty anekaśaḥ dhaninām iva veśmāni hatāny agnyanilāmbubhiḥ
english: Those priceless chariots, shattered there in their numbers, gleamed like the mansions of the wealthy ruined by fire, wind, and flood.

sanskrit: dvipāḥ saṃbhinnamarmāṇo vajrāśanisamaiḥ śaraiḥ petur giryagraveśmāni vajravātāgnibhir yathā
english: Elephants, their vital parts pierced through by arrows like thunderbolt and lightning, fell as mountain-top dwellings fall before bolt, gale, and fire.

sanskrit: sārohās turagāḥ petur bahavo 'rjunatāḍitāḥ nirjihvāntrāḥ kṣitau kṣīṇā rudhirārdrāḥ sudurdṛśaḥ
english: Many horses with their riders fell, struck down by Arjuna, their tongues and entrails hanging out, spent upon the earth, drenched in blood, ghastly to behold.

sanskrit: narāśvanāgā nārācaiḥ saṃsyūtāḥ savyasācinā babhramuś caskhaluḥ petur nedur mamluś ca māriṣa
english: Men, horses, and elephants, sewn through by Savyasācin's iron shafts, wheeled about, stumbled, fell, cried out, and wilted, good sir.

sanskrit: aṇakaiś ca śilādhautair vajrāśaniviṣopamaiḥ śarair nijaghnivān pārtho mahendra iva dānavān
english: With fine arrows whetted on stone, like thunderbolt, lightning, and venom, Pārtha struck them down as great Indra struck the Dānavas.

sanskrit: mahārhavarmābharaṇā nānārūpāmbarāyudhāḥ sarathāḥ sadhvajā vīrā hatāḥ pārthena śerate
english: Heroes in costly armor and ornaments, with garments and weapons of every kind, with their chariots and banners, lie slain by Pārtha.

sanskrit: vijitāḥ puṇyakarmāṇo viśiṣṭābhijanaśrutāḥ gatāḥ śarīrair vasudhām ūrjitaiḥ karmabhir divam
english: Vanquished, men of pious deeds, of distinguished birth and learning, they have gone with their bodies to the earth, and by their mighty deeds to heaven.

sanskrit: athārjunarathaṃ vīrās tvadīyāḥ samupādravan nānājanapadādhyakṣāḥ sagaṇā jātamanyavaḥ
english: Then your heroes rushed upon Arjuna's chariot—lords of various realms, with their troops, their wrath kindled.

sanskrit: uhyamānā rathāśvais te pattayaś ca jighāṃsavaḥ samabhyadhāvann asyanto vividhaṃ kṣipram āyudham
english: Borne by chariot-horses, and the foot-soldiers too, bent on killing, they ran at him, swiftly hurling weapons of every kind.

sanskrit: tadāyudhamahāvarṣaṃ kṣiptaṃ yodhamahāmbudaiḥ vyadhaman niśitair bāṇaiḥ kṣipram arjunamārutaḥ
english: That great downpour of weapons, hurled by those great storm-cloud warriors, the wind that was Arjuna swiftly scattered with his sharp arrows.

sanskrit: sāśvapattidviparathaṃ mahāśastraugham aplavam sahasā saṃtitīrṣantaṃ pārthaṃ śastrāstrasetunā
english: That shoreless flood of mighty weapons—with its horses, foot, elephants, and chariots—Pārtha sought all at once to cross by the causeway of his missiles and shafts.

sanskrit: athābravīd vāsudevaḥ pārthaṃ kiṃ krīḍase 'nagha saṃśaptakān pramathyaitāṃs tataḥ karṇavadhe tvara
english: Then Vāsudeva said to Pārtha: "Why do you toy with them, O sinless one? Crush these Saṃśaptakas and then make haste to the slaying of Karṇa."

sanskrit: tathety uktvārjunaḥ kṣipraṃ śiṣṭān saṃśaptakāṃs tadā ākṣipya śastreṇa balād daityān indra ivāvadhīt
english: Saying "So be it," Arjuna at once assailed the Saṃśaptakas who yet remained, and with his weapon slew them by force, as Indra slew the Daityas.

sanskrit: ādadhat saṃdadhan neṣūn dṛṣṭaḥ kaiś cid raṇe 'rjunaḥ vimuñcan vā śarāñ śīghraṃ dṛśyate sma hi kair api
english: Some saw Arjuna in the fray drawing his arrows or fitting them to the string; by others he was seen only as he loosed the shafts, so swift was he.

sanskrit: āścaryam iti govindo bruvann aśvān acodayat haṃsāṃsagaurās te senāṃ haṃsāḥ sara ivāviśan
english: Crying "A marvel!" Govinda urged on the horses; white as a goose's wing, they entered the enemy host as geese enter a lake.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃgrāmabhūmiṃ tāṃ vartamāne janakṣaye avekṣamāṇo govindaḥ savyasācinam abravīt
english: Then Govinda, gazing over that field of battle while the slaughter of men went on, spoke to Savyasācin:

sanskrit: eṣa pārtha mahāraudro vartate bharatakṣayaḥ pṛthivyāṃ pārthivānāṃ vai duryodhanakṛte mahān
english: "O Pārtha, here rages the dread destruction of the Bharatas, the great ruin of the kings of the earth, brought about for Duryodhana's sake."

sanskrit: paśya bhārata cāpāni rukmapṛṣṭhāni dhanvinām mahatām apaviddhāni kalāpān iṣudhīs tathā
english: "Behold, O Bhārata, the gold-backed bows of the great archers cast aside, and the bundles of arrows and the quivers as well."

sanskrit: jātarūpamayaiḥ puṅkhaiḥ śarāṃś ca nataparvaṇaḥ tailadhautāṃś ca nārācān nirmuktān iva pannagān
english: "And the arrows with golden nocks and bent joints, and the oil-washed iron shafts, like serpents that have shed their skins."

sanskrit: hastidantatsarūn khaḍgāñ jātarūpapariṣkṛtān ākīrṇāṃs tomarāṃś cāpāṃś citrān hemavibhūṣitān
english: "Swords with ivory hilts adorned with gold, lances scattered about, and bows bright and decked with gold."

sanskrit: varmāṇi cāpaviddhāni rukmapṛṣṭhāni bhārata suvarṇavikṛtān prāsāñ śaktīḥ kanakabhūṣitāḥ
english: "Coats of mail flung off, gold-backed, O Bhārata, and lances wrought with gold, and javelins adorned with gold."

sanskrit: jāmbūnadamayaiḥ paṭṭair baddhāś ca vipulā gadāḥ jātarūpamayīś carṣṭīḥ paṭṭiśān hemabhūṣitān
english: "And great maces bound with bands of pure gold, and pikes of gold, and spiked clubs adorned with gold."

sanskrit: daṇḍaiḥ kanakacitraiś ca vipraviddhān paraśvadhān ayaskuśāntān patitān musalāni gurūṇi ca
english: "Battle-axes with shafts bright with gold flung about, and iron-pointed goads fallen, and heavy pestles."

sanskrit: śataghnīḥ paśya citrāś ca vipulān parighāṃs tathā cakrāṇi cāpaviddhāni mudgarāṃś ca bahūn raṇe
english: "Behold the gaily-wrought hundred-slayers, and the huge iron bludgeons, and the discuses cast away, and the many hammers on the field."

sanskrit: nānāvidhāni śastrāṇi pragṛhya jayagṛddhinaḥ jīvanta iva lakṣyante gatasattvās tarasvinaḥ
english: "Grasping weapons of every kind, those swift warriors, greedy for victory, though their life is fled, seem still as though alive."

sanskrit: gadāvimathitair gātrair musalair bhinnamastakān gajavājirathakṣuṇṇān paśya yodhān sahasraśaḥ
english: "Behold the warriors by thousands—their limbs crushed by maces, their heads broken by pestles, trampled by elephants, horses, and chariots."

sanskrit: manuṣyagajavājīnāṃ śaraśaktyṛṣṭitomaraiḥ nistriṃśaiḥ paṭṭiśaiḥ prāsair nakharair laguḍair api
english: "By arrows, spears, swords, and lances, by sabres, pikes, javelins, claw-weapons, and clubs, men, elephants, and horses—"

sanskrit: śarīrair bahudhā bhinnaiḥ śoṇitaughapariplutaiḥ gatāsubhir amitraghna saṃvṛtā raṇabhūmayaḥ
english: "—with bodies hewn in many ways, awash in floods of blood, their breath gone, the battlefields are covered, O slayer of foes."

sanskrit: bāhubhiś candanādigdhaiḥ sāṅgadaiḥ śubhabhūṣaṇaiḥ satalatraiḥ sakeyūrair bhāti bhārata medinī
english: "With arms smeared with sandal paste, bearing armlets and fair ornaments, with guards on them and bracelets, the earth shines, O Bhārata."

sanskrit: sāṅgulitrair bhujāgraiś ca vipraviddhair alaṃkṛtaiḥ hastihastopamaiś chinnair ūrubhiś ca tarasvinām
english: "With finger-guarded hands and forearms flung about, all bedecked, and with the severed thighs of those swift warriors, like elephants' trunks."

sanskrit: baddhacūḍāmaṇivaraiḥ śirobhiś ca sakuṇḍalaiḥ nikṛttair vṛṣabhākṣāṇāṃ virājati vasuṃdharā
english: "With the severed heads of those bull-eyed men, bound with choice crest-jewels and wearing earrings, the earth is resplendent."

sanskrit: kabandhaiḥ śoṇitādigdhaiś chinnagātraśirodharaiḥ bhūr bhāti bharataśreṣṭha śāntārcirbhir ivāgnibhiḥ
english: "With headless trunks smeared with blood, their limbs and necks lopped off, the earth shines, O best of the Bhāratas, as if with fires whose flames have died."

sanskrit: rathān bahuvidhān bhagnān hemakiṅkiṇinaḥ śubhān aśvāṃś ca bahudhā paśya śoṇitena pariplutān
english: "Behold the chariots of many sorts, broken, fair with their golden bells, and the horses too, in many places drenched with blood."

sanskrit: yodhānāṃ ca mahāśaṅkhān pāṇḍurāṃś ca prakīrṇakān nirastajihvān mātaṅgāñ śayānān parvatopamān
english: "And the great conch-shells of the warriors, and the white whisks scattered about, and the elephants with their tongues lolling out, lying like mountains."

sanskrit: vaijayantīvicitrāṃś ca hatāṃś ca gajayodhinaḥ vāraṇānāṃ paristomān suyuktāmbarakambalān
english: "And the slain elephant-fighters bright with their banners, and the housings of the elephants, with their well-fitted cloths and woolen rugs."

sanskrit: vipāṭitā vicitrāś ca rūpacitrāḥ kuthās tathā bhinnāś ca bahudhā ghaṇṭāḥ patadbhiś cūrṇitā gajaiḥ
english: "And the gay rugs of varied figures torn apart, and the bells broken in many ways, ground to bits by the falling elephants."

sanskrit: vaiḍūryamaṇidaṇḍāṃś ca patitān aṅkuśān bhuvi baddhāḥ sādidhvajāgreṣu suvarṇavikṛtāḥ kaśāḥ
english: "And the goads with handles of beryl gems fallen to the ground, and the gold-wrought whips bound to the banner-tops of the riders."

sanskrit: vicitrān maṇicitrāṃś ca jātarūpapariṣkṛtān aśvāstaraparistomān rāṅkavān patitān bhuvi
english: "And the horse-cloths and coverings, varied and gem-bright, wrought of gold and made of antelope-wool, fallen upon the ground."

sanskrit: cūḍāmaṇīn narendrāṇāṃ vicitrāḥ kāñcanasrajaḥ chatrāṇi cāpaviddhāni cāmaravyajanāni ca
english: "The crest-jewels of the kings, the bright golden garlands, the parasols flung aside, and the yak-tail whisks and fans."

sanskrit: candranakṣatrabhāsaiś ca vadanaiś cārukuṇḍalaiḥ kḷptaśmaśrubhir atyarthaṃ vīrāṇāṃ samalaṃkṛtaiḥ vadanaiḥ paśya saṃchannāṃ mahīṃ śoṇitakardamām
english: "Behold the earth, miry with blood, strewn with the faces of heroes—faces bright as moon and stars, with lovely earrings and trimmed beards, exceedingly adorned."

sanskrit: sajīvāṃś ca narān paśya kūjamānān samantataḥ upāsyamānān bahubhir nyastaśastrair viśāṃ pate
english: "And behold the men still living, moaning on every side, tended by many who have laid down their weapons, O lord of peoples."

sanskrit: jñātibhiḥ sahitais tatra rodamānair muhur muhuḥ vyutkrāntān aparān yodhāṃś chādayitvā tarasvinaḥ punar yuddhāya gacchanti jayagṛddhāḥ pramanyavaḥ
english: "There, with kinsmen gathered round, weeping again and again, having covered over other warriors who have departed, the swift ones, greedy for victory and full of wrath, go forth again to battle."

sanskrit: apare tatra tatraiva paridhāvanti māninaḥ jñātibhiḥ patitaiḥ śūrair yācyamānās tathodakam
english: "Others, proud men, run hither and thither there, begged for water by their fallen kinsmen, the heroes."

sanskrit: jalārthaṃ ca gatāḥ ke cin niṣprāṇā bahavo 'rjuna saṃnivṛttāś ca te śūrās tān dṛṣṭvaiva vicetasaḥ
english: "And some who went for water, O Arjuna, lie breathless, many of them; and those heroes who came back, at the very sight of them, lost their senses."

sanskrit: jalaṃ dṛṣṭvā pradhāvanti krośamānāḥ parasparam jalaṃ pītvā mṛtān paśya pibato 'nyāṃś ca bhārata
english: "At the sight of water they rush forward, crying out to one another; behold, O Bhārata, some dead from drinking the water, and others still drinking."

sanskrit: parityajya priyān anye bāndhavān bāndhavapriya vyutkrāntāḥ samadṛśyanta tatra tatra mahāraṇe
english: "Others, O lover of kinsmen, forsaking their dear ones and their kin, were seen passing away here and there in that great battle."

sanskrit: paśyāparān naraśreṣṭha saṃdaṣṭauṣṭhapuṭān punaḥ bhrukuṭīkuṭilair vaktraiḥ prekṣamāṇān samantataḥ
english: "Behold yet others, O best of men, biting their lips, gazing all about with faces knit in scowling brows."

sanskrit: etat tavaivānurūpaṃ karmārjuna mahāhave divi vā devarājasya tvayā yat kṛtam āhave
english: "This deed in the great battle befits you alone, O Arjuna, or the king of the gods in heaven—what you have wrought in this fight."

sanskrit: evaṃ tāṃ darśayan kṛṣṇo yuddhabhūmiṃ kirīṭine gacchann evāśṛṇoc chabdaṃ duryodhanabale mahat
english: Thus Kṛṣṇa, showing that field of battle to the Diademed One as he drove on, heard a great clamor from Duryodhana's army.

sanskrit: śaṅkhadundubhinirghoṣān bherīpaṇavamiśritān rathāśvagajanādāṃś ca śastraśabdāṃś ca dāruṇān
english: The blare of conches and kettledrums mingled with tabors and drums, the din of chariots, horses, and elephants, and the dreadful clash of weapons.

sanskrit: praviśya tad balaṃ kṛṣṇas turagair vātavegibhiḥ pāṇḍyenābhyarditāṃ senāṃ tvadīyāṃ vīkṣya dhiṣṭhitaḥ
english: Entering that host with his wind-swift horses, Kṛṣṇa halted, beholding your army hard pressed by Pāṇḍya.

sanskrit: sa hi nānāvidhair bāṇair iṣvāsapravaro yudhi nyahanad dviṣatāṃ vrātān gatāsūn antako yathā
english: For he, the foremost of bowmen, with arrows of every kind slew the throngs of his enemies in battle, robbing them of life like Death himself.

sanskrit: gajavājimanuṣyāṇāṃ śarīrāṇi śitaiḥ śaraiḥ bhittvā praharatāṃ śreṣṭho videhāsūṃś cakāra saḥ
english: That best of strikers, piercing with sharp arrows the bodies of elephants, horses, and men, made them depart from their flesh, bereft of life.

sanskrit: śatrupravīrair astāni nānāśastrāṇi sāyakaiḥ bhittvā tān ahanat pāṇḍyaḥ śatrūñ śakra ivāsurān
english: Cutting apart with his shafts the various weapons hurled by the foremost of his foes, Pāṇḍya slew those enemies as Śakra slew the Asuras.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca proktas tvayā pūrvam eva pravīro lokaviśrutaḥ na tv asya karma saṃgrāme tvayā saṃjaya kīrtitam
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: This great hero, renowned in the world, you named before, but his deeds in battle you have not recounted, O Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: tasya vistarato brūhi pravīrasyādya vikramam śikṣāṃ prabhāvaṃ vīryaṃ ca pramāṇaṃ darpam eva ca
english: Tell me now in full the valor of that great hero—his skill, his might, his prowess, his measure, and his pride.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca droṇabhīṣmakṛpadrauṇikarṇārjunajanārdanān samāptavidyān dhanuṣi śreṣṭhān yān manyase yudhi
english: Saṃjaya said: Droṇa, Bhīṣma, Kṛpa, the son of Droṇa, Karṇa, Arjuna, and Janārdana—those masters of their craft whom you deem foremost with the bow in battle—

sanskrit: tulyatā karṇabhīṣmābhyām ātmano yena dṛśyate vāsudevārjunābhyāṃ ca nyūnatāṃ nātmanīcchati
english: —by him a parity with Karṇa and Bhīṣma was shown in himself, nor would he own himself inferior to Vāsudeva and Arjuna.

sanskrit: sa pāṇḍyo nṛpatiśreṣṭhaḥ sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ karṇasyānīkam avadhīt paribhūta ivāntakaḥ
english: That Pāṇḍya, best of kings, foremost of all bearers of arms, slew Karṇa's host like Death scorned and roused to fury.

sanskrit: tad udīrṇarathāśvaṃ ca pattipravarakuñjaram kulālacakravad bhrāntaṃ pāṇḍyenādhiṣṭhitaṃ balam
english: That force, with its surging chariots and horses, its choice foot-soldiers and elephants, beset by Pāṇḍya, whirled about like a potter's wheel.

sanskrit: vyaśvasūtadhvajarathān vipraviddhāyudhān ripūn samyag astaiḥ śaraiḥ pāṇḍyo vāyur meghān ivākṣipat
english: His foes, their horses, drivers, banners, and chariots gone, their weapons flung from their hands, Pāṇḍya scattered with well-aimed shafts as the wind scatters clouds.

sanskrit: dviradān prahataprothān vipatākadhvajāyudhān sapādarakṣān avadhīd vajreṇārīn ivārihā
english: Elephants with their trunks struck off, their pennons, banners, and weapons gone, together with their foot-guards, that slayer of foes slew as the foe-slayer slew his enemies with the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: saśaktiprāsatūṇīrān aśvārohān hayān api pulindakhaśabāhlīkān niṣādān dhrakataṅgaṇān
english: Horsemen with their lances, javelins, and quivers, and their horses too, the Pulindas, Khaśas, Bāhlīkas, the Niṣādas, and the Taṅgaṇas,

sanskrit: dākṣiṇātyāṃś ca bhojāṃś ca krūrān saṃgrāmakarkaśān viśastrakavacān bāṇaiḥ kṛtvā pāṇḍyo 'karod vyasūn
english: the southerners and the Bhojas, cruel and hardened in war—stripping them of weapons and armor with his arrows, Pāṇḍya robbed them of life.

sanskrit: caturaṅgaṃ balaṃ bāṇair nighnantaṃ pāṇḍyam āhave dṛṣṭvā drauṇir asaṃbhrāntam asaṃbhrāntataro 'bhyayāt
english: Seeing Pāṇḍya, undaunted, smiting the fourfold host with his arrows in the fray, the son of Droṇa, more undaunted still, advanced upon him.

sanskrit: ābhāṣya cainaṃ madhuram abhi nṛtyann abhītavat prāha praharatāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ smitapūrvaṃ samāhvayan
english: Addressing him sweetly, dancing forward as if without fear, that best of strikers spoke, smiling first, as he summoned him:

sanskrit: rājan kamalapatrākṣa pradhānāyudhavāhana vajrasaṃhananaprakhya pradhānabalapauruṣa
english: "O king, lotus-petal-eyed, master of the finest weapons and mounts, you whose frame seems forged of the thunderbolt, foremost in strength and manhood,"

sanskrit: muṣṭiśliṣṭāyudhābhyāṃ ca vyāyatābhyāṃ mahad dhanuḥ dorbhyāṃ visphārayan bhāsi mahājaladavad bhṛśam
english: "twanging your great bow with both long arms, your weapon clasped fast in your fists, you shine exceedingly like a great rain-cloud."
